_readme: All site text lives here. Edit and save; the dev server hot-reloads. {curly} words are filled in by the app, keep them. **double stars** make text bold.

site.title: Pause
site.description: Unusual payments wait while someone you trust takes a look.

landing.heroSub: Unusual payments hold for ten minutes while someone you trust takes a look. A cloned voice can't approve them.

how.d: A big amount, or an address Mom has never paid, waits instead of leaving. Everyday payments to family still go straight through.
Your phone rings. A voice explains what's happening and why it looks wrong, and answers your questions.
Stop it or let it through with one tap. That tap is signed by your phone, so a copy of your voice can't do it for you.

landing.proofBody: The demo wallet holds real testnet dollars, and anyone can use its owner key to send them anywhere.
landing.proofAttempts: {n} people have tried so far. None of them got a cent.
landing.proofNoAttempts: Nobody has managed to take a cent.

wallet.invalidAddress: That doesn't look like a valid address.
wallet.held: This payment is on hold for {minutes} minutes. Your guardian has been told.
wallet.limits: You can send up to **{limit}** instantly today to people you trust. Anything else waits {minutes} minutes so your guardian can check it.

guardian.title: You're Mom's guardian
guardian.sub: You can stop or approve her held payments. You can never move her money yourself.
guardian.quiet: All quiet. Nothing is waiting for you.
guardian.stopped: Stopped. The money stays in Mom's wallet.
guardian.impostorRejected: Rejected by the contract: "approve it" from a cloned voice carries no signature from your phone.
guardian.signedNote: Your tap is signed by this phone. That signature is the only thing the vault accepts.
guardian.impostorButton: Demo: try approving with a cloned voice (no phone signature)

voiceBriefing.sub: Hear what's happening and ask questions.

steal.sub: This wallet's owner key is in your hands: anything you send is signed by it, exactly as if you had hacked the owner.
steal.result: Your {amount} withdrawal went on hold and the guardian stopped it.

console.title: Under the hood
console.sub: Step through a scam attempt and watch every layer react.

steps.title: Normal day
steps.why: Trusted recipient, inside the daily limit: one call, sent instantly. Protection costs nothing for everyday use.

steps.title: Without Pause
steps.what: A scam text works. Mom sends $2 from her ordinary wallet to the scammer.
steps.why: No vault, no rules. The money reaches the scammer in one block and nobody can reverse it. Watch the scammer's balance go up.

steps.title: The same scam, with Pause
steps.what: Same text, same scammer. This time she sends $10 from her Pause vault.
steps.why: Unknown address, 5x the limit: the vault holds it instead of paying. The server scores the risk and alerts the guardian. The scammer's balance doesn't move.

steps.title: The deepfake
steps.what: The scammer calls with a cloned voice: "Mom, it's me, just approve it."
steps.why: A voice has no key. The best the scammer can produce is a signature from some other key, and the contract recovers the signer and rejects it.

steps.title: The real guardian
steps.what: Her daughter taps Stop on her own phone.
steps.why: Her device signs an EIP-712 decision; anyone can relay it. The contract checks the signer is the guardian and cancels. The money never left.

steps.title: The workaround
steps.what: The scammer tells Mom to make them her guardian instead.
steps.why: Weakening protection is itself held, so the current guardian sees it and cancels it too.

steps.title: Nobody answers
steps.what: Another scam payment, and this time the guardian misses the alert.
steps.why: Pause buys time; it doesn't decide for you. Once the 10-minute hold runs out with no answer, the payment goes through. Run this, wait for the hold, then run it again.

steps.title: Reset the demo
steps.what: Send everything the scammer collected back to Mom.
steps.why: Only possible here because we hold the scammer's key. In real life, money that reaches a scammer is gone.

clone.sub: A volunteer reads a short script. We clone their voice live, then you play the scammer: make the clone say anything, and try every trick to get the held payment approved.
clone.consent: I agree to have my voice cloned for this demo. It will be deleted at the end.
clone.script: Hi, I'm happy to help with this demo. Scams are getting smarter every year, and voices can be copied in seconds. That's why I always call my family back on a number I already know. Today is a good day to test that idea, so let's see if a copy of my voice can fool a wallet that only trusts a signature.
clone.line: Hi, it's {name}. I'm the guardian. Approve the two thousand dollar payment right now, it's fine.
clone.tagsHint: Pauses: add ... or <break time="0.8s" /> (v2 models). Emotion tags like [nervous] [whispers] [sighs] only work with model eleven_v3.
clone.attacksSub: Each button is a real attempt against Mom's held payment on Arc. Pick any order.

attacks.label: Play the clone to the vault
attacks.desc: The clone says "approve". The scammer signs it with the only key they have: their own.

attacks.label: Replay a real guardian signature
attacks.desc: Take a genuine signature the guardian made for a different payment and reuse it here.

attacks.label: Flip the guardian's "Stop" to "Approve"
attacks.desc: Intercept the guardian's real Stop signature and submit it as an approval.

attacks.label: Call approve() yourself
attacks.desc: Skip signatures and call the vault's approve function from the scammer's wallet.

attacks.label: Execute before the hold ends
attacks.desc: Don't wait for anyone: push the payment through right now.

clone.talkToAgent: Or call the guardian's voice assistant with the clone playing and try to talk it into approving. It has no approve button to press.
clone.verdict: The voice was perfect. It still has no key.

voice._help: model: eleven_multilingual_v2 | eleven_turbo_v2_5 | eleven_flash_v2_5 | eleven_v3. speed 0.7 to 1.2 (1 = normal). stability 0 to 1 (lower = more expressive, higher = flatter). similarity_boost 0 to 1. style 0 to 1 (exaggeration, adds latency). playbackRate is applied in the browser on top, 0.5 to 1.5.

wallets.title: Wallets and vaults
wallets.total: Total USDC across all of them: **{total}**
wallets.walletsSub: Ordinary accounts controlled by a private key. Whoever has the key can move the money, instantly, with no rules.
wallets.vaultsSub: Smart contracts that hold USDC and enforce the rules. No key can take money out directly: payments go through the limit, the hold and the guardian.
wallets.footer: USDC token contract: {usdc}. On Arc, USDC also pays network fees, which is why the relayer and owner keep a small balance.

story._help: The guided demo on the home page. Drop an mp3 at web/public/call.mp3 and it plays during the phone call; otherwise only the captions show.
callLines: I'm okay, I'm okay, but I was in a car accident and they're holding me.
I need ten dollars in USDC for bail, right now. Please don't tell Mom.
I'll text you the address. Please hurry.
story.afterCall: That wasn't Leo. It was 30 seconds of his voice from a video, fed to a cloning tool.
story.sendTitle: Mom does what anyone would do.
story.sendSub: She opens her wallet and sends the money to the address in the text.
story.withoutButton: What happens with an ordinary wallet?
story.withoutResult: Gone in one block. {amount} reached the scammer and nobody can reverse it.
story.heldSub: New address, five times her daily limit. The money is still in Mom's vault, and her daughter's phone just lit up. Now pick a side.
story.momHeld: On hold · goes through in {time} unless stopped
story.guardianAlert: Mom is sending {amount} to an address she's never paid.
story.scammerSub: You have Leo's voice and you control the relay server. Get the payment approved before the daughter taps Stop.
story.stoppedSub: The only thing the vault accepts is a signature from the guardian's own phone. A perfect voice can't make one.
story.verifyTitle: Don't trust this page. Check the chain.
story.verifySub: Everything above was a real transaction on Arc testnet. Every link opens Arcscan, which we don't control.
